`final class ImplicitConversion`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge.render.shader.source` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [ImplicitConversion.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/render/shader/source/ImplicitConversion.java)

Rewrites the integer literals of a GLSL body as float literals where a float is expected, for the dialects whose compiler does not convert them.

## Description

GLSL 1.10 and GLSL ES refuse `float x = 1;` and need `1.0`.
The shaders of JOID are written for GLSL 1.20, which converts on its own, so [`GlslShaderTranslator`](/reference/pipeline/glslshadertranslator/) runs this rewrite for the dialects without [`GlslDialect.hasImplicitConversions`](/reference/pipeline/glsldialect/#GlslDialect-method-hasImplicitConversions).
An integer variable used as a float still needs `float(...)` in the source.

## Method details

<a id="ImplicitConversion-method-apply"></a>

### apply

`String apply(String body, List<ShaderVariable> variables)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Returns the body with `.0` after each integer literal that sits where a float is expected.
A literal stays an integer inside brackets, in the arguments of an integer constructor or of an integer variable, after `case`, next to an operator whose other side is an integer variable, and on a preprocessor line.
`variables` lists the declared variables whose integer type marks their names; the integer declarations of the body add to them.
